and supports features for executing payments, canceling payments, issuing refunds, capturing two-stage payments, creating and canceling subscriptions for recurring payments, and sending invoices via email. _API
Parameters are sent via the POST method either as
pairs in the request body or in JSON format.
The API can accept no more than 150,000 fields per single request. API response timeout: 5 minutes.
In all requests to the API, if you pass a floating-point number into an integer field, the API does not return an error; instead, mathematical rounding will be applied automatically.

The API limits the maximum number of concurrent requests to 5 for test terminals and to 30 for production terminals. If the number of requests currently processed exceeds the limit, the API returns a 429 HTTP status code (Too Many Requests) until at least one request has finished processing. If you need to revise these limits, contact your account manager.

is used as the password. Both values can be obtained from the dashboard.
If the request does not include an authentication header or contains incorrect authentication data, the system returns a 401 HTTP status (Unauthorized).
The API Secret is used for security. It must be stored in a secure location. _API

is an API property that ensures that a repeated request returns the same result as the initial request without being processed again. This means that you can send multiple requests to a system with the same ID, only one successful request will be processed, and all responses will be identical. This mechanism protects against network errors that could otherwise result in duplicate records or actions.
header containing a unique ID in your API request. You generate this request ID. It can be a GUID, a combination of the order number, date, and amount, or any other value at your discretion.
Each new request that requires processing must include a unique
value. The processed result is retained in the system for 1 hour. _API

You can use the secure request authentication mechanism for payouts. To do this, provide our support team with a certificate containing your public key. Next, generate a signature based on the request body and include it within the X-Signature header in base64 format. CloudPayments will verify your signature using CryptoService. If the signature is valid, the request processing will proceed; otherwise, the execution will be terminated.
